note: Rewritten from entry 89 in Roonwal & Chhotani (1997), the original in English. The original describes only the soldier and worker, the alate being recorded as unknown. The original gives the soldier antennal segment count as "9-segmented", which conflicts with the generic diagnosis (soldier 13–19 segments) and is probably an OCR misreading; that number has not been adopted, only the account that segment 2 is shortest and segment 3 club-shaped being retained. The synonymy list, literature citations, figure numbers, type-specimen records and distribution records have been omitted.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head length to mandibular base 2.15–2.45 mm, width 1.35–1.55 mm, antennae stouter, segment 2 larger, ratio of the postmentum waist width to its maximum width 0.37–0.40; it differs from the comparably sized dunensis, in which the antennae are thinner, segment 2 smaller and that ratio 0.47–0.55. Alate unknown.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule and antennae reddish brown, posterior part of the head yellowish brown; mandible apex nearly black, base reddish brown; abdomen yellowish white. Head and pronotum sparsely hairy, body moderately hairy. Body length about 6.10–6.50 mm. Head capsule rectangular, distinctly longer than wide (length to mandibular base 2.15–2.20, width 1.35–1.40 mm); sides nearly parallel, slightly narrowed in front of the antennal sockets; posterior margin rounded; frons sloping forwards; Y-suture faintly visible, its posterior arms reaching the occiput. Fontanelle small, oval, white, situated in the anterior 1/3 of the head. Antennal segment 2 shortest, segment 3 club-shaped, darker and longer than the remaining segments. Eyes small, white, adjacent to the antennal sockets; ocelli minute, their distance from the eye greater than the long diameter of the eye. Postclypeus indistinctly delimited from the frons, with a few hairs, anterior margin straight; anteclypeus white, narrow, anterior margin slightly convex. Mandibles stout and rather long (length 1.25–1.35 mm), more than half the head length (mandible length to head length ratio 0.58–0.63). Labrum ligulate, wider than long (length 0.15–0.23, width 0.35–0.38 mm). Postmentum 1.15–1.65 mm long, club-shaped, the anterior and posterior lobes of the club each further lobed, the lower lobe wider (0.50–0.55 mm), then narrowing into a long waist (0.20 mm). Pronotum flat, nearly trapezoidal, wider than long (width 1.15–1.20, length 0.70–0.75 mm), with a translucent median line; anterolateral corners acute, anterior margin concave with a deep median notch, posterior margin convex, without a notch. Femora short, stout and swollen, tibiae slender, tibial spur formula 3:2:2, tarsi 3-segmented. Abdomen elongate, hairy; cerci 2-segmented, 0.13 mm long; abdominal styli absent.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule, postclypeus and antennae yellow, labrum and mandibles yellowish brown, body paler. Head moderately hairy, body rather densely hairy. Body length 3.80–4.90 mm. Head capsule nearly circular, slightly wider than long (width 1.10–1.30, length to mandibular base 0.90–1.15 mm); Y-suture distinct. Fontanelle small, oval, almost in the middle of the head. Eyes rather large, visible in strong light. Antennae 13–14-segmented; segment 2 nearly as long as segments 3 and 4 together, segment 4 shortest. Postclypeus slightly swollen, nearly trapezoidal, median line indistinct. Anteclypeus narrow, trapezoidal. Labrum wider than long, anterior margin rounded. Mandibles as in the generic diagnosis. Pronotum flat, wider than long (width 0.85–0.93, length 0.48–0.55 mm); anterior margin slightly concave, posterior margin with a distinct median emargination. Legs and abdomen as in the soldier.
